explanation: A net ionic equation strips a reaction down to only the species that actually change. You start from the molecular equation (AgNO3 + NaCl -> AgCl + NaNO3), write every strong electrolyte as its separated aqueous ions (the complete ionic equation), then cancel the ions that appear unchanged on both sides — the spectator ions Na+ and NO3-. What remains, Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> AgCl(s), is the net ionic equation. On the AP exam you must produce balanced net ionic equations for precipitation, acid-base, and redox reactions and justify why a species is a spectator; charge and mass must both balance.
bullets: Only ions that change phase or bond stay: Ag+ and Cl- form solid AgCl.
Na+ and NO3- are spectators — present before and after, so they cancel.
The arrows show reacting ions converging to form the precipitate.
A correct net ionic equation balances both atoms and total charge.
